title: “Looks human, communicates warmly”: the impact of chatbots' anthropomorphic design cues on users' intention to adopt health information
abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine how anthropomorphic design cues in healthcare chatbots, specifically appearance and communication style, influence users' intention to adopt health information through perceived competence and perceived warmth in low-to moderate-risk health contexts. Design/methodology/approach Drawing on the persuasion knowledge model, elaboration likelihood model, stereotype content model and computers are social actors, we develop a research model and conduct two online experiments. Study 1 adopts a 2 × 2 between-subjects design with 352 participants to examine the effects of anthropomorphic appearance (with vs without human names and avatars) and communication style (task-oriented vs social-oriented) on users' adoption intention through perceived competence and warmth. Study 2 employs a 2 × 2 × 2 factorial design with 473 participants to validate the findings and examine the moderating roles of persuasion knowledge and health literacy. Findings The results indicate that anthropomorphic appearance enhances perceived competence and warmth. A task-oriented communication style increases perceived competence, whereas a social-oriented style enhances perceived warmth. Both perceived competence and warmth significantly increase users' adoption intention and mediate the effects of anthropomorphic appearance and communication style on adoption intention. Additionally, persuasion knowledge weakens the effects of anthropomorphic appearance but does not moderate the relationship between communication style and perceived warmth. Health literacy negatively moderates the relationship between perceived warmth and adoption intention, while positively moderating that between perceived competence and adoption intention. Originality/value This study extends existing research by simultaneously examining anthropomorphic appearance and communication style in healthcare chatbots and uncovering the underlying psychological mechanisms through which these cues influence users' adoption intention. title: Twin Cohorts Using Linked Administrative Data: A Rapid Review
abstract: Abstract Twin research is increasingly integrating administrative data, from hospital, birth, and education registers, to understand human behavior, health, and disease. This includes administrative data to supplement existing twin-cohort databases or to identify new twin cohorts from only administrative datasets. We conducted a rapid review to identify twin cohorts that were collecting linked administrative data. We searched the Medline database and the Atlas of Longitudinal Cohort Studies for such twin studies. This included twin studies either linking data to pre-existing cohorts or studies identifying twin cohorts in administrative data. We identified 117 manuscripts or profiles featuring 47 unique twin cohorts and two multicohort consortia using linked administrative data, from countries across most global regions. We summarize how these cohorts were established, the data collected, and the size of the cohorts. We then discuss opportunities, challenges, and future research in twin research using linked administrative data.

title: Translational laboratory medicine and interdisciplinary biomarker discovery in sepsis: bridging molecular insights and clinical decision-making
abstract: Abstract Sepsis remains a major global health burden characterized by high mortality and diagnostic uncertainty. Advances in laboratory medicine have made it a central field in translational biomarker discovery, integrating molecular biology, bioinformatics, and clinical sciences. This review summarizes recent evidence with a focus on the translational trajectory from biomarker identification to clinical implementation, including protein biomarkers, cellular biomarkers, and RNA profiling. Emphasis is placed on patient phenotyping approaches, multi-marker strategies, integrating multidimensional parameters from different biological systems by modern classifiers, and the evolving role of laboratory medicine as an interdisciplinary nucleus for improving sepsis diagnosis and prognostication.

title: The influence of construction business resilience and brand integrity on building crisis management strategies in the construction industry
journal: International Journal of Disaster Resilience in the Built Environment
abstract: Purpose This study aims to investigate the influence of construction business resilience (CBR) and brand integrity (BI) on crisis management strategies (CMS) and their significance in the construction industry. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research design was used, with data collected from 205 industry stakeholders via structured questionnaires. Multiple regression analysis evaluated the impact of CBR and BI on CMS, highlighting key relationships and trade-offs. Findings CBR is strongly and positively associated with CMS (B = 1.292, β = 0.971, p < 0.001), underscoring the importance of resilience capabilities in maintaining operational continuity during disruptions. By contrast, BI shows a negative association with CMS (B = −0.405, β = −0.305, p < 0.001), suggesting that reputation-related concerns can, in some contexts, temper or slow visible crisis responses rather than straightforwardly enhancing them. Research limitations/implications The use of a purposive, non-probabilistic sample of contractors, consultants and client representatives, skewed towards individuals with fewer than five years of experience, means the findings cannot be generalised to the entire Ghanaian construction industry and may reflect particular perceptions of crises and resilience. Practical implications Construction firms should integrate resilience into their operations by using early warning systems, conducting risk assessments and embracing technological advancements. Policies must prioritise stakeholder engagement, disaster preparedness and financial resilience to ensure a balance between BI and effective crisis response. Originality/value This study offers a new, integrated examination of CBR, BI and CMS within the Ghanaian construction industry, emphasising a context-contingent negative association between BI and crisis management responses.

title: The effect of particle size on techno-functional properties and biscuit quality of chickpea flour: a simple additive weighting (SAW) approach
abstract: Abstract The particle size of flours plays a crucial role in enhancing their functionality by influencing surface area and the exposure of active sites, which in turn may improve solubility, dispersibility, and broaden their potential for various food applications. Therefore, in the present study, chickpea flour was prepared with five different particle sizes to develop biscuits. The effect of particle size on water and oil absorption capacity, bulk density properties, foaming capacity, swelling power and dispersibility of chickpea flour was investigated. In terms of particle size of flours, chickpea flour with the largest particle size (400 µm) showed the highest water absorption capacity at all substitution levels, outperforming the finer flour particles. Foaming capacity of chickpea flours with varying particle sizes ranged from 17.45 % to 30.42 %. Notably, the flour with a 200 μm particle size showed the highest foaming capacity, suggesting that this size is ideal for formulating protein-enriched foods that require aeration in their texture, such as cakes, ice cream and confectionery products. The fracturability values of the biscuit samples ranged from 22.7 mm to 23.88 mm, with a clear trend indicating that the breakability increased as the flour particle size increase. In terms of the particle size of the flours, chickpea flour with the largest particle size (400 μm) showed the highest water absorption capacity at all substitution levels, leaving behind finer flour particles. In terms of texture, the CF200 sample, which exhibited the lowest hardness value, also demonstrated the best overall textural properties, making it suitable for producing more desirable biscuit textures. Sensory analysis using the SAW technique revealed that the CFUS sample was the most preferred in terms of general acceptability, while the CF400 biscuit was the least favored. This study will provide a theoretical basis for the production of superior chickpea-based products in the food industry and will contribute to the production of high value-added products.

Work–home interaction and flourishing: The sequential mediating role of social connectedness and positive coping
abstract: Orientation: Knowledge workers navigating hybrid and digitally mediated work environments face heightened work-to-home interaction (WHI) demands that may influence their capacity to flourish. Research purpose: This study examined whether workplace social connectedness (WSC) and positive coping behaviour (PCB) sequentially mediate the relationships between four WHI sub-dimensions and flourishing among South African knowledge workers. Motivation for the study: Although flourishing is a key indicator of optimal functioning, limited research has explored how WHI influences flourishing through underlying social and personal resource mechanisms. Examining WSC and PCB as sequential mediators provides insight into these processes. Research approach/design and method: A quantitative, cross-sectional survey design was employed. Data were collected from a convenience sample of 427 South African knowledge workers using validated measurement instruments. Hayes’s PROCESS Macro (Model 6) was used to test sequential mediation effects. Main findings: Negative WHI and negative home-to-work interaction (HWI) were directly and negatively associated with flourishing. While total indirect effects were generally non-significant, specific indirect pathways emerged. Negative WHI was associated with lower flourishing through reduced WSC, whereas negative HWI was associated with lower flourishing through reduced PCB. For positive WHI, WSC independently mediated the relationship with flourishing, and a small but significant sequential indirect effect through WSC and PCB was observed. No indirect effects were found for positive HWI. Practical/managerial implications: Organisations should strengthen employees’ proactive coping capabilities and foster meaningful workplace connections to support resilience and well-being in hybrid work environments. Contribution/value-add: This study extends understanding of how social and personal resources relate to flourishing under competing work–home demands. The findings highlight the limited but meaningful role of sequential mediation in positive WHI and provide insights for human-centred human resource management practices aligned with Industry 5.0.
